codeReview.summary: The feature adds the enhancement endpoint, route sampling, and Google API integrations, but it does not fully enforce the generic-title-only rule and can repeatedly re-spend API budget for activities that fail POI discovery, which violates strict cost-control intent.

issues.description: When `activityId` is provided, the endpoint processes that activity without verifying the title matches the allowed generic pattern. This violates the requirement to only enhance Morning/Afternoon/Evening/Lunch/Night Ride titles and can overwrite non-generic names.

Activities with no discovered POIs are skipped without persisting any terminal state, so subsequent batch runs will recompute Google Geocoding/Places calls for the same activity indefinitely. This undermines strict cost controls and the no-recompute intent.
UI uses `alert(...)` for enhancement results, violating AGENTS.md convention forbidding browser dialogs for UX/testing reasons.

sharedStateObservations.observation: The worker's `skillFeedback.followedProcedure` is marked true, but transcript evidence shows deviations from `fullstack-worker` procedure (implementation before tests and no agent-browser manual verification).
sharedStateObservations.evidence: Transcript skeleton (worker session 8e46a4cb-1142-476a-af71-0df095ef84c4) shows Create/Edit calls on implementation files before test creation and only curl-based interactive checks; no agent-browser tool usage is present.

sharedStateObservations.observation: Route-prefix behavior between local dev server and function router caused repeated confusion and rework; this endpoint-prefix expectation is not clearly captured in shared library docs.
sharedStateObservations.evidence: Transcript shows repeated endpoint attempts (`/api/activities/...` then `/api/api/activities/...`) and edits/restarts in `functions/src/dev-server.ts` to reconcile mounting behavior.

summary: Review failed due to two blocking requirement gaps: generic-title enforcement is bypassed for explicit `activityId` requests, and no-POI activities are repeatedly recomputed across batch runs, risking uncontrolled API spend.
